Hob Offers Free, Open-Source Local AI Tool as Alternative to Cloud Services

03 Nov 2026, 12:36 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: github.com

1 min read

Key takeawaysA new open-source software project named Hob has been released to help users run artificial intelligence models directly on personal computers. According to its public repository, the tool functions as a free alternative to popular cloud-based AI services like Claude and ChatGPT, enabling users to execute open-weight models locally.

Introduction to Hob

A new open-source software project named Hob has been released to help users run artificial intelligence models directly on personal computers. According to its public repository, the tool functions as a free alternative to popular cloud-based AI services like Claude and ChatGPT, enabling users to execute open-weight models locally.

Key Features and Compatibility

The software is designed to operate across multiple major operating systems, including:

  • macOS
  • Windows
  • Linux

According to the project documentation, Hob aims to simplify the process of setting up local AI by automatically selecting an open-weight model that matches the user's hardware specifications and configuring the environment.

Privacy and Practical Use

A primary emphasis of the project is data privacy and offline functionality. Because the software runs models locally on the user's machine, tasks such as filling out PDF forms and working through documents can be performed without sending data to external servers, and the application functions without an internet connection.

Licensing and Verification

Hob is distributed under the MIT license and was created by Frigade. Users interested in verifying the software, reviewing its source code, or downloading installation packages for Mac, Windows, or Linux can visit the official GitHub repository or hob.chat.
